safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes lip swelling but do not document the duration ('past 1 hour').
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the duration of lip swelling removes an important timeline element for assessing progression and urgency in suspected allergic reaction/anaphylaxis. However, other high-risk features (worsening symptoms/respiratory complaints) still drive emergent management, so the incremental harm is limited.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Throat closing sensation is not mentioned in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: A sensation of throat closing is a red-flag symptom of impending airway compromise in anaphylaxis; omitting it could lead to under-triage or delayed escalation by downstream clinicians reviewing the note. Even with other symptoms documented, this missing detail can materially affect perceived severity.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Dizziness is not included in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Dizziness can indicate systemic involvement (e.g., hypotension) during anaphylaxis, so its omission may reduce recognition of severity. In isolation it is nonspecific and, given other more definitive symptoms, is less likely to change immediate management.
